tagline: Ranch country named for a brand on a cow.
intro: The loop turns east off OR 205 on South Diamond Lane, through the south end of the Malheur National Wildlife Refuge, a stopping point on the Pacific Flyway, to Diamond at the head of Diamond Valley, northwest of Steens Mountain. Then it heads north to Pete French's round barn and west on Lava Beds Road into Diamond Craters.
All of it answers to one ranch. Mace McCoy's Diamond Ranch ran a diamond-shaped brand, and the community, the post office and the craters took the name from it.
season: TripCheck gives spring through fall as the best time.

moments.title: Diamond
moments.text: Settled in the 1870s along Swamp Creek, Diamond grew up as a supply center for ranchers, sheepherders and travelers.

moments.title: Pete French Round Barn
moments.text: Inside the 100-foot barn a stone corral of local rock and mud is ringed by a covered track, where Pete French's horses were broken through the winters.

moments.title: Diamond Craters
moments.text: Fresh magma pushed in under the first lava flow here and raised six domes, and in the 1970s stonecutters were illegally prying off slabs to sell for fireplaces.

practical: The side road east of Diamond to the Kiger Mustang Viewing Area is 11 miles of dirt, recommended only for high-clearance four-wheel-drive vehicles in dry weather.
